baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C10_DISCOVERY_SSH_TRUST_ENROLLMENT_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN, 2026-09-15). Its own model, restated for a second vendor and a second key shape rather than reopened: an unverified endpoint identity is never silently trusted and never blindly refused -- the operator is shown what was observed, explicitly authorizes it once, and the product remembers that authorization per endpoint. C10's schema (management_endpoint_ssh_trust) is SSH-host-key-shaped by design (key_algorithm, ssh key fingerprint) and is vendor-locked to CHECK_POINT by its own CHECK constraint; this movement does not alter that table or that constraint. It builds the same pattern as a sibling table shaped for an X.509 certificate fingerprint, for Palo Alto.
baseline.engineering: AGENTS.md's Palo Alto section: 'Production TLS requires trusted corporate CA verification. Historical POC TLS-verification exceptions are technical debt, never production design.' This movement does not create a bypass or a POC exception: it keeps NXS-LOCAL-0359's chain verification exactly as the first, default check, and adds an explicit, audited, per-device operator authorization as the second path for a certificate that cannot chain to a trusted root -- the identical shape C10 already established and that this constitution already accepts for Check Point. No certificate is ever accepted silently.
baseline.observed: NXS-LOCAL-0359 (merged) replaced PanXmlApiTransport's name-matching certificate check with real chain verification, which is correct and stays. What it exposed: every enumerated Palo Alto firewall in this environment presents its own default, self-signed certificate -- not one issued by the corporate CA that verifies Panorama's own certificate. All 39 currently-enumerated PAN devices report FAILED with a distinct, correct fingerprint each. The only existing escape hatch, PAN_DISCOVERY_TRUST_PINNED_FINGERPRINT_SHA256, is a single global environment variable: it can pin exactly one fingerprint, never 39 distinct per-device ones, so it cannot be the real mechanism here. The Product Owner's direction, given directly in this session: this is exactly the trust-once-then-remember model C10 already built for Check Point SSH host keys, and Palo Alto needs the same thing, not a bypass.

invariants: No certificate is ever trusted silently: chain verification or an explicit, audited, per-device operator enrollment -- there is no third path

recommended_reasoning.reason: A new trust-store schema and its audit trigger, plus a worker-side trust-resolution change and a UI enrollment flow, all mirroring an already-frozen, already-proven pattern for a second vendor -- bounded by precedent, but touching a security boundary.

requirements: A certificate that verifies by chain (the corporate CA case) never needs enrollment and is unaffected by this movement
A certificate that cannot verify by chain is rejected until the operator explicitly enrolls its exact fingerprint for that management address and port
An enrolled fingerprint is stored per device, never applied globally to every Palo Alto device

A later connection presenting a different fingerprint than the one enrolled is rejected, not silently re-trusted -- re-enrollment is its own explicit action, exactly as C10 already requires for Check Point
Every enrollment and re-enrollment is audited: who, when, what was observed, matching C10's existing audit shape
The environment-variable pinned-fingerprint path keeps working unchanged for whoever still relies on it
risks: This is a new table and a new pair of gated actions, not a schema change to the existing CHECK_POINT-locked table -- do not widen management_endpoint_ssh_trust's vendor CHECK constraint to fit Palo Alto; that table's shape (SSH key_algorithm) does not fit a certificate anyway.

Do not let the new per-device store silently override a certificate that already verifies by chain -- chain verification stays first and is not bypassed for a device that happens to have a stored (and now unnecessary) trust entry.
This is a Gradle checkout: use ./gradlew, not mvn.

The frontend test runner needs node_modules, which a fresh worktree does not carry. If npm test or tsc cannot start, link or install ui2/frontend dependencies in the worktree and run them; do not report BLOCKED with the work unvalidated.

39 already-enumerated Palo Alto devices exist in the live environment with FAILED collection state and a known fingerprint each -- this movement's job is to make enrollment possible, not to enroll any of them; that is the Product Owner's own action once this ships.

in: A new migration: management_endpoint_pan_cert_trust, shaped like management_endpoint_ssh_trust (trust_entry_id, management_address, management_port, fingerprint_sha256, status ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED, authorized_by, authorized_at, observed_at, superseded_by), vendor fixed to PALO_ALTO, with the same append-only-history audit trigger pattern C10 already uses -- a new table, not a change to the CHECK_POINT-only management_endpoint_ssh_trust

A new gated action pair (enroll / re-enroll) and two new endpoints, POST /discovery/pan-trust/enroll and POST /discovery/pan-trust/re-enroll, mirroring the existing ssh-trust ones exactly in shape and gating

PanXmlApiTransport / EnvironmentPanTrustRuleResolver: before falling back to the environment-variable pinned fingerprint (kept for compatibility, not removed), look up a stored ACTIVE trust entry for the device's management address and port; if the presented certificate's fingerprint matches the stored one, trust it -- otherwise still verify by chain first, exactly as NXS-LOCAL-0359 already does

A frontend enrollment step in the PAN add/discovery flow, presenting the observed fingerprint and requiring the operator's explicit confirmation, mirroring the existing SSH trust step in AddDeviceDialog.tsx
Tests for a first enrollment, a fingerprint mismatch on re-enroll, chain-verified certificates bypassing enrollment entirely (unchanged NXS-LOCAL-0359 path), and the endpoint gating
out: Any change to management_endpoint_ssh_trust, its CHECK_POINT constraint, or the Check Point trust flow
Any change to NXS-LOCAL-0359's chain-verification logic itself -- it stays the first, default path
Removing or weakening the PAN_DISCOVERY_TRUST_PINNED_FINGERPRINT_SHA256 environment escape hatch -- it stays as a deploy-time override, unrelated to this per-device store
Bulk-trusting multiple devices from one action, or auto-enrolling a certificate without an explicit per-device operator action
PAN authentication transport convergence, discovery parsing, or anything about what is collected once a connection succeeds
